description:
## Why
fz-nhb.11 makes the parser read Elixir's `(A, B -> R)` beside fz's own `(A, B) -> R`. Two spellings of one type is a concept added; this ticket removes the extra one.

## What changes
- Every `(..) -> ..` function type outside parentheses in lib/*.fz (116 spec/type lines on 248d23229), fixtures and guides is rewritten as `(.. -> ..)`.
- `parse_paren_or_arrow` refuses a `->` after the closing `)` with a spanned diagnostic naming the Elixir spelling.
- `term` is a builtin type that resolves to the same Ty as `any`, as in Erlang/Elixir (erl_internal is_type(term, 0); dialyzer erl_types from_form term -> t_any()).
- Every spec type variable is declared in `when`, as Elixir requires (decision, owner, 2026-11-17): `v: var` when used two or more times, `v: term()` when used once. On origin/develop 14470768a that is 195 lib specs (257 `var`, 22 `term()`) and 15 fixture specs (13 `var`, 6 single-use). fz then refuses, with Elixir's wording and a span, an undeclared type variable ("type a/0 undefined") and a `var` used once ("type variable a is used only once ... equivalent to term()").
- Measured: the same lib rewrite with `any` in place of `term()` passes the whole workspace suite (6976 passed, 0 failed, no pin moved), so a once-used variable bounded by `term()` is the unbounded variable fz already had.
- Fixture 01080: both specs declare `a` (`when a: term()`), the fixture is wrapped in defmodule M/Main with `# oracle: self`, and its twin is deleted.

## Signal
No `) ->` function type remains in lib, fixtures or guides; no undeclared or once-used `var` type variable remains; each refusal has a diagnostic fixture; 01080 is its own oracle; full gate green.

## Collision
lib/*.fz is edited by other sessions (Optimize, fz-engine R2); sequence through the coordinator.
title: One function-type spelling: lib specs use Elixir's (A, B -> R) and fz's (A, B) -> R is retired
